seats.achievable: partial - four sequenced units (US1327, US1328, US1329 in wave one, then US1330, 18 points) cover every clause, and every Fails-on I sampled is true at HEAD, but two things can sink the cut: the open-bug count has only three of headroom (46 open, bar is under 50) while the run's own reviews file findings, so the bar clause is not within the batch's control; and US1328 AC5 asks for a 'New in 6.5' line inside README's 1,500-word ceiling when README is 1,498 words, so the builder must cut existing prose that the Affects list does not make explicit.
seats.done_means: Serves O10 (Abena Osei, End goals 1 and 2: a change board gets one evidence pack and honest specs, with every number tied to a decision of record) and O9 (Jonah Reyes, End goal 4: a 6.4 project upgrades with the path stated), and Rowan Achterberg End goal 3 (a release a consuming team can upgrade to: boundary green, every known issue named, changelog complete). Done means US1327 to US1330 are Done with their executable ACs green, v6.5.0 exists in every version home, the CHANGELOG section is cut by release_cut.py, docs/known-issues.md states D0560's bar and shows it met at the cut commit, and docs/evidence.md lists RPT0045.
seats.one_increment: yes - one epic, one release, one reader (Abena at the change board); the three paperwork units are independent of each other in content and US1330 declares Depends on all three. They share README, prd.md, trd.md, tsd.md and changelog.d, so they land serially, not in parallel. The cut must be last, which the dependency enforces.
seats.note: Spot-checks at 21fe2bec9: docs/release-notes-v6.5.0.md absent; README has no 'New in 6.5' line and is 1,498 words; package.json at 6.4.0; docs/existing-users.md has no 'From 6.4 to 6.5'; prd.md, trd.md, tsd.md hold none of persona_review.py, --red-run, --distinct-from, persona-reviews, mutation-edits, CI Red Runs; tools/known_issues.py BARS tops out at v6.0; docs/evidence.md lacks RPT0045. Claims the code supports: mutation.py has --edits, gate.py has --red-run, file_finding.py has --distinct-from, persona_resolve.py has the standard, gate.py checks pyyaml; 139 bugs name D0564 and 128 name D0613, matching the stories; open bugs are 46, all Low (known_issues.py bar exits 0). Findings: (1) US1329 AC1 requires the PRD to say no script reads ci.wait_timeout_minutes 'while BG1613 is open'; BG1613 is an open Low, and if any unit fixes it first the sentence turns false, and the code does read the key in test_ci_wait_config only, so the unit should assert BG1613 is open at the cut or drop the clause. (2) US1327 AC2 and US1330 AC2 both touch the disclosure count line: the notes must carry exactly one filled line and no other open count, so US1327 must leave it as a placeholder and US1330 fill it, and the AC wording should say so. (3) The release bar is at risk from this run's own filings: with 46 open, four findings or more reach 50; the plan should say new findings from this batch are fixed in-unit (the standing rule) before the cut. (4) US1328 README word ceiling as above. (5) Not checked by execution: the claim that test_lean_docs_v64's froms[:4] breaks with a 6.5 heading above 6.4 was run at grooming and I did not re-run it.

seats.done_means: Serves O10 (Abena Osei, End goals 1, 2 and 3: the change board passes the release on the evidence the run produced, with an accountable name and a cost per point read from signed reports), with O4 (Maya Okafor, End goal 4: specs, notes and code reconciled) and O9 (Jonah Reyes, End goal 4: the 6.4 upgrade path given as commands with judgement calls reported) and Rowan Achterberg End goal 3 (a release a consuming team can upgrade to: boundary green, every known issue named, changelog complete). seats.one_increment: yes - one release epic, one outcome: a coherent v6.5.0 release commit. Wave one (US1327, US1328, US1329) touches disjoint files, and the cut (US1330) depends on all three and shares files with each, so it must land last and alone. seats.note: Spot checks by execution at 21fe2bec9, all read-only. (1) The goal as worded names no outcome; the cut and the paperwork serve O10 and Abena End goals 1 to 3, as the stories' Serves lines say. (2) No criterion asks a page to state something the code does not do, and the stories pre-empt the known cases: US1054's changelog fragment still says a copy naming 'the Primary persona, Sam the new shopper' is refused (changelog.d/US1054.md lines 10 and 11), BG1655 made that no claim, and US1330 AC1 and US1327 AC3 both require it corrected before the cut; BG1613 (ci.wait_timeout_minutes has no reader, Open, Low) is named by US1327 AC4 and US1329 AC1 as a thing the pages must say, and test_ci_wait_config.py is the only script file that mentions the key. (3) Watch items, not blockers: the 'at or above 6.5.0' and 'judged at the commit that cut' phrasing keeps the Verify lines true at later gates, but US1327 AC5 and AC2 read figures from the bug corpus and decisions at test time, so run twenty-seven's own filings and Won't Fix rulings can move them; the cut must be the last commit of the run; the three persona-review-owed lines the cut prints are advice, not a refusal, and the operator should decide whether to take the persona reviews before the tag. (4) Headroom: four bugs of slack under the 50 bar. Brief reviewers to fix, not file, any Low they find inside a unit (the file-skill-frictions rule), and to file nothing Medium that is not fixed in the run.
